liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Foolish Heart** (2 reviews): Short, with a Mydland solo mid-song leading into a Garcia solo section; Reviewer singles out it as a second-set opener, alongside To Lay Me Down [12][15]
- **Iko Iko** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the opener fairly ordinary, but the show grows steadily more intense; Reviewer says the band came out of the gate sharp and ready [14][15]
- **Peggy-O** (2 reviews): Reviewer hears it as a strutting performance from Jerry's guitar, following Greatest Story; Reviewer praises a powerful opening run of Iko, Greatest Story and Peggy-O [15][21]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Reviewer finds it very powerful, giving goosebumps; recommends listening loud and uninterrupted [11]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Tuning is audible beforehand, and Brent and Jerry exchange words between verses [13]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Reviewer says the band lifts it higher in the second extended jam [16]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Reviewer groups it with Foolish Heart, Looks Like Rain and The Wheel as making a great second set [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-04-13 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-13 t02 Iko Iko**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-13 t03 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-13 t04 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-13 t05 It's All Over Now**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-13 t06 To Lay Me Down**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-13 t07 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd89-04-13 t08 Don't Ease Me In**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-04-13.140991.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 137 min [1]
- **gd1989-04-13.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83769.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 132 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Band sounds clean, crisp and relaxed on this recording [16]
- **gd1989-04-13.152345.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 19 songs; 131 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1989-04-13.154422.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 131 min [4]
- **gd89-04-13.sbd.nawrocki.5607.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 129 min; rated 3.64/5 by 11 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer rates the recording quality good, around 4 out of 5, for this soundboard; Somewhat muffled sound, but every player is audible; Reviewer hears the sound as muffled, as if covered by a thick sheet [11][12][13][17][21]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended the 4/11 show but missed this one; their copy has Peggy-O rather than El Paso [11]
- Reviewer reached the front row on Phil's side, where the bass was physically overwhelming [12]
- Reviewer calls this the final show of the Rosemont run; the track labeled El Paso is actually Peggy-O [13]
- Reviewer attended, recalls little, and mentions watching a memorable sunrise afterward; part of a Chicago run [14]
- Reviewer got in on a miracle after driving to Chicago with a friend, arriving in the lot around two [19]
- Encore was moved to the end of the first set so the show fits on two discs [2]
- Reviewer says this Chicago run is rarely discussed among the strong 1989 shows [14]
- Reviewer gives four stars since the band climbed higher later in 1989; Brent is playing wildly here [16]
- Reviewer says even the more ordinary 1989 shows shine, agreeing with earlier reviewers [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-04-13.140991.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100 deck); Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics, ortf (OTS); Transfer Info: Master PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM… [1]
- **gd1989-04-13.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83769.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [2]. Also: Audience tape on Nakamichi 300/CP4 with Sennheiser 441 mics, to cassette master then CD; thanks to Scotton and Walker for tapes; Patch source was recorded by Steve Cherson; a brief cut occurs in Don't Ease Me In [2]
- **gd1989-04-13.152345.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 25, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [3]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several masters were combined to make the show complete [3]
- **gd1989-04-13.154422.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 25, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [4]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy, with multiple masters combined; this is a 16-bit conversion of the 24-bit 96k transfer [4]
- **gd89-04-13.sbd.nawrocki.5607.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > Dat > CDR > EAC > CDWave > mkwACT [6]
